chunks: And from them, from Sa'd, from Al-Haytham ibn Abi Masrūq Al-Nahdī, from 'Ali ibn Asbāṭ, from some of our companions, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allāh, the Blessed and Exalted, begins by looking at the visitors of the grave of Al-Ḥusain (peace be upon him) on the eve of 'Arafah. I asked, 'Before He looks at the people of the station (of 'Arafah)?' He said, 'Yes.' I asked, 'How is that?' He said, 'Because among those (people of 'Arafah) are illegitimately conceived children, and among these (visitors of Ḥusain) there are no illegitimately conceived children.'

key_terms.زُوَّارِ قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ: Visitors of the grave of Al-Husain

ai.seo_question: Why does God look at the visitors of Imam Husain's grave before the pilgrims of Arafah?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) highlights the unique spiritual status of Ziyārah to Imām Al-Ḥusain (peace be upon him) by noting that Allāh gazes upon its visitors before the pilgrims at Mount Arafah. This precedence is attributed to the purity of lineage among the visitors, contrasting with the presence of 'children of fornication' among the general Arafah pilgrims, a concept rooted in Shia exegetical traditions regarding the specific spiritual merit of the Ahl al-Bayt's devotees.
